steps.do: Print the darkMode setting from the Tailwind config file.
Build the minified production CSS from the input stylesheet.
Count how many times the border-gray-600 class appears in the built CSS, which should be at least 1.

K-002395.example: The config line reads darkMode: 'class', and the build prints Done in 312ms. The grep count for border-gray-600 in dist/out.css is 1 because the minified file is a single line.
K-002395.check: The grep prints darkMode: 'class', the build exits with no error, and the border-gray-600 count is 1 or more.
traps: Small models write dark: classes but leave darkMode unset, which defaults to media and makes the class toggle do nothing. Tailwind v4 replaces darkMode with an @custom-variant dark rule, so check the…

steps.do: Run the focus-state test for dark inputs.
In the test, press Tab to focus the input and read the ring color from its computed box-shadow.
Compare the ring color to the dark background and require a ratio of at least 3:1.
Typecheck the input component props so the variant classes are validated.

K-002396.example: The class dark:focus:ring-blue-400 (#60a5fa) against #1f2937 measures about 5.6:1, which passes 3:1. The class focus:ring-blue-500 (#3b82f6) on the same background measures about 3.8:1, which also passes.
K-002396.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, the ratio assertion is 3 or higher, and tsc exits with no output.
traps: Small models check only text contrast and skip the focus ring. WCAG 2.2 requires focus indicators at 3:1 against adjacent colors. The ring offset color must also match the dark background.

steps.do: Start the dev server if it is not already running.
Run the Lighthouse accessibility audit on the dark fixture page and save the JSON report.
Print the color-contrast audit score from the saved report.
Print the overall accessibility category score from the saved report.

K-002397.example: The color-contrast score prints 1 for the dark fixture page. The overall accessibility score prints 0.98, which is above the 0.95 gate.
K-002397.check: jq prints 1 for color-contrast and the overall accessibility score is 0.95 or higher.
traps: Small models run Lighthouse on the light route and treat the score as covering dark mode. The dark class must be applied before the audit, or the result describes the wrong theme. Each dark route nee…

steps.do: Check that the stylesheet declares color-scheme for the dark theme.
Run the Playwright test that emulates the dark OS color scheme.
In the test, call page.emulateMedia with colorScheme set to dark, then read the input computed background and color-scheme.
Confirm the computed background is rgb(31, 41, 55) and the computed color-scheme is dark.

K-002398.example: With emulateMedia set to colorScheme dark, the input computes to rgb(31, 41, 55) and color-scheme to dark. Without the emulation, the background stays rgb(255, 255, 255).
K-002398.check: grep prints a color-scheme line that includes dark, and Playwright prints 1 passed.
traps: Small models assume emulateMedia adds the dark class and skip testing the media strategy. color-scheme also controls native controls like the date picker and scrollbars, so setting only the backgroun…

steps.do: Find existing focus styles in the global stylesheet and the card component.
Decide the focus outline is at least 2px solid and contrasts at least 3:1 against the card background.
Decide body text inside the card reaches at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background.
Check the outline declarations in the card file for removed or thin focus rings.
Run the Playwright focus test that tabs to the card and checks the outline is visible.

K-002399.example: The plan uses outline 2px solid #1d4ed8 with outline-offset 2px, which is above 3:1 on white. Body text at #374151 on white is above 4.5:1, so both text and focus rules pass.
K-002399.check: rg prints an outline line with 2px in Card.svelte, and npx playwright test tests/card-focus.spec.ts reports 1 passed.
traps: Setting outline none without a replacement removes the focus indicator entirely.
A pale gray ring can look visible yet fail the 3:1 non-text contrast requirement.

steps.do: Find the id attributes already set in the card to locate the title element.
Decide the card root uses svelte:element with an aria-labelledby attribute pointing at the title id.
Decide the id comes from a titleId prop declared with $props and given a default value.
Check the component for Svelte type and compile errors.
Run axe on the cards page to confirm the region rule passes with a name.

K-002400.example: The card receives titleId through $props and sets aria-labelledby to titleId on the article root. A screen reader announces the title Spring sale when focus enters the card.
K-002400.check: npx svelte-check --threshold error reports 0 errors, and npx axe reports 0 violations for the region rule.
traps: Using a hardcoded aria-label drifts away from the visible title when content changes.
Setting aria-labelledby to an id that is not in the same rendered page leaves the card without a name.

steps.do: List every heading already on the page to find the current outline levels.
Read the card component to see which heading tag it renders today.
Decide the card title uses one level below its nearest section heading, such as h3 under an h2 section.
Make the heading level a prop so the parent page sets it through the Svelte 5 $props rune.
Count heading tags in the card to confirm exactly one title heading per card.
Run axe on the cards page and confirm 0 heading-order violations.

K-002401.example: The card renders h3 when the parent passes level 3 under an h2 section, so the outline goes h1, h2, h3 with no skipped level. The rg count of 1 confirms the card has a single title heading.
K-002401.check: rg -c prints 1 for Card.svelte, and npx axe on the cards page reports 0 heading-order violations.
traps: Small models often hardcode h2 in every card, which skips levels on pages that use h4.
Do not use a div with a class for the title, because a div has no heading role for screen readers.

steps.do: Find interactive elements inside the card markup to see what would nest.
Decide one primary link in the title and stretch it over the card with CSS instead of wrapping the card in an anchor.
Decide secondary buttons stay outside the stretched area and sit above it with position relative and z-index 1.
Write the stretched link rule so the ::after pseudo-element covers the card with position absolute and inset 0.
Run axe on the rendered cards page to check for nested interactive controls.

K-002402.example: The card keeps one anchor with class card-link around the title and stretches it with an ::after rule that covers the card. The Save button sits above that layer with position relative and z-index 1, so it stays clickable.
K-002402.check: rg prints exactly one anchor line in Card.svelte, and npx axe reports 0 violations for the nested-interactive rule.
traps: Wrapping the whole card in an anchor that also contains buttons nests interactive elements, which is invalid HTML.
Adding onclick to a plain div gives no keyboard access, so the div needs a real link or button.

steps.do: List every img element the card renders.
Decide content images take alt text from the data prop, and purely decorative images use an empty alt.
Decide the alt text comes through a string prop named alt, typed in the $props destructuring.
Check that no img tag lacks an alt attribute, printing any that do.
Run axe on the cards page to confirm the image-alt rule passes.

K-002403.example: The card renders img with src set to image.src and alt set to image.alt ?? '', so a missing description becomes an empty decorative alt. The product photo passes the alt Blue ceramic mug from its data prop.
K-002403.check: The rg -P command prints no lines, and npx axe reports 0 violations for the image-alt rule.
traps: Leaving the alt attribute off entirely fails the image-alt rule.
Using a filename like IMG_2231.jpg as alt text gives screen reader users no meaning.

steps.do: Find the button styles inside the card to see current sizes.
Decide every card action button has min-width and min-height of 44px.
Decide adjacent action buttons keep at least 8px of space between them.
Check the current sizing declarations in the card stylesheet.
Run the Playwright size test that measures each action button's bounding box.

K-002404.example: The plan sets the card-action class to min-width 44px and min-height 44px with an 8px gap between buttons. The Like and Share buttons measure 44px tall in the test instead of 28px.
K-002404.check: rg shows min-height: 44px in Card.svelte, and npx playwright test tests/card-targets.spec.ts reports 2 passed.
traps: Setting only padding does not guarantee the target reaches 44px because the content may be shorter.
Enlarging only the icon leaves the clickable hit area small.

steps.do: Find the existing color rules the card will reuse or replace.
Choose an error text color and confirm it reaches at least 4.5:1 against the card background.
Choose an invalid border color and confirm it reaches at least 3:1 against the field background.
Record both chosen values as custom properties in the plan.
Confirm the stylesheet has no hardcoded hex values for these states.

K-002405.example: Error text uses #b00020 on #ffffff, a ratio of about 7.3:1, which passes the 4.5:1 minimum. The invalid border uses the same red, which also clears the 3:1 minimum against the white field.
K-002405.check: The plan lists two color tokens, each with a ratio of at least 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for borders written beside it.
traps: Checking contrast only for the text and forgetting the border that signals the invalid state.
Choosing a light red that passes for large text but is used for 14px messages that fail at 4.5:1.
Planning colors without a ratio number means the build stage has nothing to verify against.

steps.do: Set the input height target to at least 44px so taps land reliably.
Set the input font-size to 1rem so mobile browsers do not zoom in on focus.
Find the existing font-size rules the card should replace.
Plan the error message at 1rem or larger so it stays readable.
Confirm the existing min-height rules, if any, are listed for replacement.

K-002406.example: The plan sets input min-height to 44px and font-size to 1rem, which is 16px at the default root size. The grep shows an old input rule at 14px, so the plan marks it for replacement.
K-002406.check: grep -n 'font-size' styles.css shows the old 14px value, and the plan marks it for replacement with 1rem.
traps: Setting input font-size below 16px triggers iOS zoom when the field gains focus.
Assuming 1rem equals 16px fails if the site changes the html font-size, so check the root value.
Planning a 44px height but leaving padding that shrinks the tappable area is a common oversight.

steps.do: Decide whether errors show after the field loses focus with :user-invalid, or only after submit.
Search the form files for novalidate, since it turns off native browser validation messages. The search should print no lines.
Search the stylesheets for the pseudo-class the plan will use. The count should print at least 1 once styles are written.
Run the form's validation tests with Playwright to confirm that required fields stay neutral on first load and show an error after blur.
Record the timing choice and the reason in the plan notes.

K-002407.example: The plan uses :user-invalid so a required field stays neutral until the user leaves it empty. The novalidate search returns no matches, the stylesheet count prints 1 or more, and the Playwright run reports 0 failed tests.
K-002407.check: rg -n novalidate -g '*.html' prints no lines, and npx playwright test tests/form-validation.spec.js reports 0 failed tests.
traps: Styling :invalid alone colors required fields red on first page load.
Adding novalidate silently removes the browser's built-in validation messages.
Choosing submit-only errors without a plan for live feedback leaves users waiting for a failed submit to learn what is wrong.

steps.do: Check that React 18 or later is installed so the useId hook is available.
Find any existing use of useId in the source tree.
Decide that the error element gets an id derived from the input id, such as email-error.
Decide that role alert is used only for submit errors, not on every keystroke.
Confirm the plan lists aria-invalid and aria-describedby on the input element.

K-002408.example: The Input component calls useId to build an id, sets aria-describedby to that id when an error exists, and renders the message in an element with role alert only after submit. npm ls react should print a version of 18.0.0 or higher.
K-002408.check: npm ls react prints a version of 18 or higher, and the plan lists aria-describedby and aria-invalid as required attributes.
traps: Do not use role alert on every keystroke, because it floods screen readers with announcements.
Do not hardcode a static error id, because two inputs on one page would share it.
npm ls exits with code 1 when a package is missing, so read the exit code before assuming React is present.

steps.do: Read package.json to confirm the test script and the test runner in use.
Run the type checker and note its exit code.
Run the unit test suite once in non-watch mode without any changes.
Count the test files that cover input components.
Write the baseline results in the plan so later failures can be traced to the right change.

K-002409.example: npx tsc --noEmit exits 0 with no output, and npx vitest run reports 41 passing tests before any edit. find lists 1 file named Input.test.tsx.
K-002409.check: npx tsc --noEmit prints nothing and exits 0, and npx vitest run ends with a Tests line showing 0 failed.
traps: Do not skip the baseline, because later failures from old code will look like new bugs.
Do not run a test command in watch mode, because it never exits.
Do not ignore a nonzero exit code from tsc.

steps.do: List the test files that already exist for form inputs.
Check whether Testing Library for React is installed as a dev dependency.
Check whether Playwright is installed for end-to-end runs.
Write one test name per state: empty, blur-invalid, submit-invalid, server-error, and recovered.
Set the timing bound that the error message must appear within 200ms of blur.

K-002410.example: Input.test.tsx gets 5 named cases, one for each state, and the Playwright check requires the blur error to render within 200ms. npx playwright --version prints the installed version number.
K-002410.check: npm ls @testing-library/react prints the installed version, find lists the existing test files, and the plan contains exactly 5 named test cases.
traps: Do not plan only the happy path, since empty and error states are the goal.
Do not name tests with vague words like works, because the name should state the input and the expected result.
A timing bound with no test that measures it is not a check, so name the command that enforces it.

steps.do: List every React file that renders an input element.
Count how many of those files already set aria-invalid.
Find existing Input wrapper components by filename.
Check whether a wrapper already accepts an errorMessage prop.
Run the existing Playwright suite in list mode and record the total test count, then record the file paths and both counts in the plan before writing code.

K-002411.example: rg -l lists 12 files with input tags and rg -c finds aria-invalid in 3 of them, so the plan adds it to the other 9 forms. The Playwright list reports 40 tests as the baseline. The plan names src/components/Input/Input.tsx as the single wrapper to extend.
K-002411.check: rg -l prints one path per file, find prints Input.tsx, npx playwright test --list prints a total such as 40 tests, and the plan note states both counts, for example 12 and 3.
traps: Do not assume no wrapper exists without running find.
rg -c prints one count per file, so add the counts together before reporting a total.
Do not write component code in the plan stage.

steps.do: Find the existing fetch calls that submit the form.
Check the shape of errors the API returns, such as field keys in the response body.
Write a map from each server field key to the matching input name.
Decide that the typed value is kept after a server error so the user does not retype it.
Run the conflict test with a timer and confirm the field error appears within 200ms of the response.

K-002412.example: A 409 response with errors containing a username key maps to the username input, which sets aria-invalid and shows the message taken below it. The plan keeps the typed value and lists 1 handled field key. The Playwright run reports the field error at 140ms, under the 200ms limit.
K-002412.check: The rg output lists the API file path, the plan note includes a key map with at least 1 entry and states that the input value is preserved, and the Playwright run shows the error within 200ms.
traps: Do not clear the field after a server error.
Do not show a server error only as a toast, because it hides which field failed.
Do not treat a 500 response as a field error.

steps.do: Create the unit test file tests/unit/AppToast.spec.ts and import mount from @vue/test-utils.
Mount AppToast with the prop state set to loading.
Assert the root element has the attribute role equal to status and aria-live equal to polite.
Run the unit test file with Vitest.
Confirm the Vitest summary reports zero failed tests.

K-002413.example: The spec mounts AppToast with state loading and reads wrapper.attributes("role") to get status. It then reads wrapper.attributes("aria-live") to get polite.
K-002413.check: Vitest prints Test Files 1 passed and Tests 3 passed with 0 failed.
traps: Small models often skip aria-live polite because they think role status is enough, but the spec must assert both attributes.
Do not assert only on a spinner CSS class, since that proves nothing about screen readers.

steps.do: Create the end to end test file e2e/toast-loading.spec.ts using Playwright.
Click the save button and wait for a role status element with a 200ms timeout.
Run only this end to end test file.
Show the Playwright HTML report for any failing timing check.

K-002414.example: The test clicks the button with name Save profile and calls expect(page.getByRole("status")).toBeVisible({ timeout: 200 }). A slow render fails the assertion with a timeout error after 200ms.
K-002414.check: Playwright prints 1 passed with a duration below 2s for the test file.
traps: Small models set the timeout to 2000 and call the check passing, but the target is 200ms.
Do not use waitForTimeout with a fixed delay, because it hides whether the toast rendered in time.

steps.do: Add a unit test named replaces loading toast that resolves a mocked promise.
Run only the test whose name matches replaces loading toast.
Count the toast elements in the DOM after flushPromises completes.
Check the source file for the single role status region in the template.

K-002415.example: The test mocks saveProfile to resolve after one tick, calls await flushPromises, then asserts document.querySelectorAll(".toast").length equals 1. The grep count of role status in AppToast.vue should equal 1.
K-002415.check: Vitest prints 1 passed and the grep prints 1, with the test count of toast elements equal to 1.
traps: Small models count toasts before the promise settles, which gives a false pass with two elements.
Do not accept a count of 2 as correct, since a stale loading toast must be removed.

steps.do: Start the Vite dev server in the background on port 5173.
Open the demo page that shows the loading toast in a browser.
Run the axe command line scanner against the demo page URL.
Confirm the scanner lists no color-contrast violations for the toast text.

K-002416.example: The loading text color is #595959 on #ffffff, a ratio of 7:1, which passes. A lighter gray such as #9a9a9a on white gives about 2.8:1 and fails the 4.5:1 minimum.
K-002416.check: The axe output prints 0 violations for the color-contrast rule on the toast-demo page.
traps: Small models assume a spinner is decorative and skip its text contrast, but the message text must reach 4.5:1.
Do not run axe before the dev server responds on port 5173, or it scans an error page and reports a false pass.

steps.do: Run the Vue type checker across the project without emitting files.
Check the exit code of the type checker and confirm it is zero.
Search the output for any line that starts with error TS to confirm there are none.

K-002417.example: AppToast defines props with state typed as the union loading or success or error. A caller that passes state set to pending fails with an error TS2322 message naming the prop.
K-002417.check: The command prints nothing and exits with code 0, so the output contains 0 lines beginning with error TS.
traps: Small models ignore warnings and treat a non-zero exit as a finished task, but any error TS line means the types are broken.
Do not use any to silence an error on the state prop, since that hides the loading state union.

steps.do: Create the test file src/components/AppToast.test.ts, then add a unit test named clears timer on unmount that mounts the toast and then unmounts it.
Add vi.useFakeTimers() before mounting so timers are tracked.
Run only the unmount test with Vitest.
steps.cmd: npx vitest run -t "clears timer on unmount"

steps.do: Confirm the test asserts that vi.getTimerCount returns 0 after unmount.

K-002418.example: The test mounts AppToast with state loading, calls wrapper.unmount, then expects vi.getTimerCount() to equal 0. A timer left running after unmount makes the count 1 and fails the test.
K-002418.check: Vitest prints 1 passed, and the assertion expect(vi.getTimerCount()).toBe(0) holds.
traps: Small models forget to call vi.useFakeTimers before mounting, so the count reads 0 even with a live timer.
Do not call vi.runAllTimers to clear the timer before the assertion, because that hides the leak.

steps.do: List the color components stored in the color set for light and dark.
Compute the contrast ratio for the light-mode pair with the contrast script in the tools folder.
Compute the dark-mode pair the same way.
Record the printed ratio for each pair. Each must be at least 4.5 for body text.

K-002419.example: Light mode text #1C1C1E on #FFFFFF gives about 16.1:1, and dark mode #F2F2F7 on #1C1C1E gives about 14.8:1, both above the 4.5:1 minimum.
K-002419.check: Both script outputs show a ratio of 4.5 or higher.
traps: Checking only the light appearance and assuming dark mode is also readable.
Testing with the system accent color instead of the actual foreground token.
Using 3:1, the large-text threshold, for body text in the modal.

steps.do: List the number inputs that feed the chart.
Run the spec that submits -5 and 101 and expects :invalid on both fields.
Run the render-count spec to confirm the chart did not redraw after the invalid submit.
Confirm the number of invalid fields reported matches the expected count of 2.

K-002420.example: The max-value field has min=0 max=100 step=5, and the spec enters -5 and 101, so both match :invalid. The spec expects 2 invalid fields and 0 chart redraws.
K-002420.check: The range spec prints '1 passed', and the render-count spec prints 'expected 0 redraws, received 0'.
traps: Small models assume type=number alone blocks bad input, but it allows out-of-range numbers until submit.
Check checkValidity() or the :invalid state, not just the visible error text.
Do not test only the happy path with 50, because that never triggers the constraint.

steps.do: Find the CSS rule that sets the error text color.
Trigger an error state on the chart form, then run axe against the page limited to WCAG 2.1 AA rules.
Compare the error color against its background and confirm the ratio is at least 4.5:1.

K-002421.example: The field-error color is #b00020 on a #ffffff background, which gives a ratio of about 7.0:1 and passes. A #ff8a80 color on white gives about 2.1:1 and fails.
K-002421.check: axe reports 0 violations under color-contrast, and the calculated ratio is 4.5:1 or higher.
traps: Small models pick a red that looks readable and skip the number, but light red on white usually fails 4.5:1.
Axe only tests rendered states, so the error must be visible before the scan runs.
Do not test the default state, where no error text is shown yet.

steps.do: List every element that has aria-describedby in the chart form.
List every element that has aria-invalid in the chart form.
Run the spec that submits an empty series field and checks aria-invalid is true.
Count the lines that mention series-error to confirm the id exists once and is referenced once.

K-002422.example: The series input has aria-describedby set to series-error, and the element with that id holds the text 'Enter at least one value'. The spec expects aria-invalid to be true after an empty submit, and rg counts 2 lines for series-error.
K-002422.check: The Playwright spec prints '1 passed', and rg -c prints a count of 2, one for the attribute and one for the id.
traps: Small models point aria-describedby at an id that does not exist, which silently does nothing for screen readers.
Setting aria-invalid without updating the message leaves the state unexplained to the user.
Do not delete the visible error text when adding the id, because sighted users need it too.

steps.do: Find the min-height rules for buttons and inputs in the chart controls CSS.
Run the spec that measures each control's bounding box at a 390px wide viewport.
Confirm every control's height and width are at least 44px.

K-002423.example: The add-series button measures 36px tall at 390px width, so its CSS needs min-height: 44px. After the fix, the spec reads 44px or more for all 7 controls.
K-002423.check: The spec prints '7 controls at least 44px' and '1 passed'.
traps: Small models add padding to the text but not min-height, so the rendered box stays short.
Measure the rendered bounding box, not the CSS value, because padding and borders change the result.
Checking only a desktop width hides the problem on phones.

steps.do: Confirm the validation handler is attached to the input event in the chart script.
Run the timing spec that types into the series field and records the time until aria-invalid changes.
Compare the longest measured latency with the 200ms budget.

K-002424.example: The series input runs its checks on each input event, and the spec records 84ms from keystroke to aria-invalid set to true. The budget is 200ms, so 84ms passes.
K-002424.check: The spec prints 'max validation latency 84ms' or a lower value, and it fails if any measurement exceeds 200ms.
traps: Small models debounce with a long setTimeout and then miss the 200ms budget.
Use the input event, because the change event fires only on blur and would miss live feedback.
Measure until the aria-invalid attribute changes, not until a spinner disappears.

steps.do: Find every setCustomValidity call in the chart script.
Run the unit test that checks a duplicate series name sets an error and a unique name clears it.
Run the browser spec that submits the form and confirms checkValidity returns true for all fields.
Confirm the custom error text is an empty string after a valid entry.

K-002425.example: Entering 'Sales' twice calls setCustomValidity with 'Name already used' on the second field. Changing it to 'Returns' calls setCustomValidity with an empty string, so checkValidity returns true.
K-002425.check: node --test prints 'pass 2' and 'fail 0', and the Playwright spec prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models call setCustomValidity once for the error but never reset it to an empty string, so the field stays invalid.
Run the custom rule before the value changes, or the duplicate check reads stale data.
Forgetting reportValidity() after a failed check leaves the user with no visible message.

steps.do: Check whether a debounce helper is already installed.
Pick a 300ms debounce window and write it into the plan file.
Confirm no debounce dependency is already listed.
Name the cancel mechanism as an AbortController held in a ref named controller.

K-002426.example: grep -n lodash package.json prints nothing, so the plan uses a 300ms setTimeout wrapper. Each keystroke calls controller.abort() before creating a new AbortController.
K-002426.check: grep -c prints 0 when no debounce helper exists, and the plan names a 300ms window.
traps: Do not plan a 0ms debounce, since it fires on every keystroke. Do not skip cancellation, because a stale response can overwrite a newer one.

steps.do: Check that the installed Vue version supports defineModel and useId.
Plan defineModel for the value so v-model works without a manual prop and emit pair.
Plan useId from vue to generate the id that links label, input, and status.
Count existing manual modelValue uses to see what the plan replaces.

K-002427.example: node -p prints 3.5.13, so defineModel and useId are available. The wrapper uses const model = defineModel<string>() and const id = useId().
K-002427.check: node prints a version of 3.5 or higher, and rg lists the modelValue files to replace.
traps: Do not plan defineModel on Vue 3.3 or earlier, where the macro does not exist. Do not build ids with Math.random, because server rendering then mismatches the client.

steps.do: List existing min-height values to find the current baseline.
Set the input min-height to 44px and the spinner to 1rem in the plan.
Count the button elements in Vue files that need the same 44px rule.
Record the plan numbers in PLAN.md beside each element.

K-002428.example: rg prints min-height 32px for the old input, so the plan raises it to 44px. The 1rem spinner fits inside the 44px row with padding on each side.
K-002428.check: rg prints the baseline heights, and the plan lists 44px for the input and every button.
traps: Do not assume 1rem always equals 16px, because it follows the root font size. Do not shrink the tap area to match a small icon; keep the 44px box and add padding.

steps.do: Confirm the Vue version so you only plan APIs it supports.
List every Vue file that renders a native input element.
Count the files that already reference a loading flag.
Create PLAN.md to hold one table row per file from the list.
Count the lines in PLAN.md. N rows plus a header and a separator line means N+2 lines.

K-002429.example: rg -l "<input" src -g "*.vue" prints SearchField.vue and EmailField.vue, so the plan lists 2 gaps. A vue entry of 3.5.13 in package.json means useId is available. wc -l PLAN.md then reports 4 lines.
K-002429.check: wc -l PLAN.md reports N+2 lines, where N is the number of files printed by rg -l.
traps: Do not assume a BaseInput wrapper covers every input; count raw input tags. Do not plan Vue 2 options-style APIs such as this.$emit or Vue.set.

steps.do: Locate existing live regions so the plan does not add a duplicate.
Check whether aria-busy is already used, so the plan sets it on the input while pending and false otherwise.
Check existing aria-live attributes before planning one status div with role status and aria-live polite beside the field.
Run axe on the dev server page to confirm the pending text meets the 4.5:1 contrast minimum with zero color-contrast violations.

K-002598.check: wc -l prints a number of at least 10 followed by the filename, and each rg -c step prints a count of at least 1 for its term.

steps.do: Confirm the loading widget test file exists.
Find the 200ms delay constant in the form source.
Count the test pumps that advance exactly 200ms before checking for the spinner.
Run only the test named spinner within 200ms and confirm it reports one passing test.

K-002599.example: lib/forms/signup_form.dart:31 sets _spinnerDelay to Duration(milliseconds: 200), and test line 44 pumps that exact duration before it looks for the spinner. The grep count of 1 confirms there is one such pump.
K-002599.check: rg prints lib/forms/signup_form.dart:31, grep -c prints 1, and the flutter test output reports +1: All tests passed!

steps.do: Find the 20px SizedBox that wraps the spinner in the form source.

find.byType(CircularProgressIndicator) can match several spinners on the page, so use the key.

K-002601.check: rg -n prints lib/forms/signup_form.dart:61, grep -c prints 1, and the flutter test final line reads All tests passed!

steps.do: List the files under Sources that mention Menu.
Count Text(verbatim:) calls in the menu view. The count must be exactly 0, because verbatim text skips localization.
Count NSLocalizedString calls in the menu view. The count must equal the number of menu labels that call it.
Read the file and confirm each Button and Text label is a string literal, not an interpolated variable.

K-002602.example: In Sources/Menu/MenuView.swift, Button("Export PDF") is safe because its key is in the catalog, but Text(verbatim: item.title) is not. The verbatim count must be 0, and the NSLocalizedString count must equal the number of menu labels that call it.
K-002602.check: grep -c -F verbatim: prints 0, and the file list from the first command includes MenuView.swift.
traps: Text(verbatim:) looks like a normal Text call but disables localization. Small models often accept it without counting. A String held in a variable is never translated, so trace each label's source.

steps.do: Count plural variation blocks in the catalog. The count must be at least 1.
Search the menu code for %lld. The command must print nothing, because the count is passed through the catalog.
Count few-form blocks, which Russian and Polish need in addition to one and other. The count must be at least 1.
Count many-form blocks, which Russian and Polish also need. The count must be at least 1.

K-002603.example: The key %lld items has English one and other forms, so 1 item and 3 items both read correctly. The grep for %lld in Sources/Menu prints nothing, because the count is passed through the catalog.
K-002603.check: The first grep prints a number of at least 1, the %lld grep prints nothing, and the few and many counts are each at least 1.
traps: Russian and Polish need more than two plural forms, so an entry with only one and other is incomplete there. Check every target language. Interpolating a count into Text in Swift bypasses plural rule…

steps.do: Confirm the shared scheme passes the double-length launch argument. The output must show the line with YES.
Count lineLimit modifiers in the menu view. The count must be 0, because a lineLimit of 1 hides longer translations.
List fixed-width frame modifiers. A label with a 180-point English width must have a frame of at least 234 points, which is 180 times 1.3.
List truncationMode modifiers. Each label that can truncate must have one, so the full text stays reachable.
Launch the app in the pseudo-language scheme and confirm no menu label is clipped at 1.3 times its English width.

K-002604.example: The scheme line shows -NSDoubleLocalizedStrings YES, and the lineLimit count is 0, so no label is cut off. A row labeled Export PDF at 180 points should grow to about 234 points under pseudo-localization without clipping.
K-002604.check: The grep prints the launch argument line, the lineLimit count is 0, the frame width is at least 234 points, and the pseudo-language run shows no clipped labels at 1.3 times width.
traps: Pseudo-localization only shows clipping when the flag is on, so an English-only run proves nothing. A lineLimit of 1 with no truncation mode hides text instead of wrapping it.

steps.do: Count physical .left padding uses in the menu view. The count is the number of hits to fix.
Count physical .right padding uses in the same file. The count is the number of hits to fix.
Edit each hit by hand to .leading or .trailing. Do not use search and replace, because .left also matches other names.
Rerun the .left count. It must print exactly 0.
Confirm a preview forces right-to-left by listing where layoutDirection is set. A line must set rightToLeft.

K-002605.example: Padding written as .padding(.left, 12) becomes .padding(.leading, 12), so the Arabic menu puts the gap on the trailing side. After the change the .left count is 0 and the .right count is 0.
K-002605.check: Both .left and .right counts print 0, and the layoutDirection grep shows a line setting rightToLeft.
traps: Physical edges like .left and .right stay fixed when the layout flips, so text lands against the wrong edge. Use leading and trailing for anything that follows reading order. A directional icon such …

Count .formatted calls, which use the current locale by default. The count must be at least 1.
Count preview blocks that set a locale. The count must be at least 2, one for German and one for Arabic.
Launch the app with an Arabic locale. The date label must show Arabic-Indic digits and contain 0 Latin digits from 0 to 9.

K-002606.example: A menu item using Date.now.formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .omitted) renders as Nov 4, 2026 in English and in a German-ordered form in German. The DateFormatter count must be 0, and the .locale preview count must be at least 2.
K-002606.check: The DateFormatter count prints 0, the .formatted count is at least 1, the .locale preview count is at least 2, and the Arabic label contains 0 Latin digits.
traps: A fixed dateFormat string shows the same layout in every language, so use Date.FormatStyle through .formatted instead. The .environment(\.locale) setting changes only the view subtree it is applied t…

steps.do: In the handler for Input.Changed, check event.validation_result.is_valid and set the error Label text to empty when it is True.
Write a test that types an invalid value, then types a valid one, and asserts the error Label text equals empty text.
Run only the clear test and confirm the summary reads exactly '1 passed' with 0 failed.
Count the lines that set the error Label text in app.py, expecting 2 lines, one for the error and one for the reset.

K-002607.example: After typing an invalid email then a valid one, event.validation_result.is_valid becomes True, and Label#error-email text is set to empty text. The pytest summary prints '1 passed', and rg -c update app.py prints 2.
K-002607.check: pytest summary prints exactly '1 passed' with 0 failed for the clear test, and rg -c update app.py prints 2.
traps: Do not clear the error on Input.Submitted only, because the message would stay visible while the user is typing a fix.
Do not clear the error by deleting the Label widget, because the test and later updates then fail to find it.
Do not compare validation_result to the string 'valid', because it is a ValidationResult object with an is_valid property.

steps.do: In the submit handler, loop over the fields in order and call focus on the first Input whose validation fails.
Write a test in tests/test_focus.py that presses enter with two blank fields and asserts that the focused widget id is name, the first field.
In the test, call await pilot.pause(0.2) before reading the error Label text, and assert the text is 'Name is required.'
Run only the focus test file and confirm the summary reads exactly '1 passed' with 0 failed.
List the lines that contain pause in the focus test, expecting exactly 1 line with the 0.2 value.

K-002608.example: Two blank fields name and email are on screen, and pressing enter focuses Input#name and shows its error after await pilot.pause(0.2). The pytest summary prints '1 passed', and rg -n pause tests/test_focus.py prints one line containing pause(0.2).
K-002608.check: pytest summary prints exactly '1 passed' with 0 failed, and rg -n pause tests/test_focus.py prints 1 line containing pause(0.2).
traps: Do not focus the last field, because the user reads the form from the top and the first error is the one to fix.
Do not use time.sleep in the test, because it blocks the Textual event loop. Use await pilot.pause(0.2) instead.
Do not assume 200ms is enough on a slow machine without a retry. Keep the wait at 0.2 and fail the test if the error is missing.

steps.do: Confirm the RTL layout test file exists.
Run the RTL layout test with Playwright.
Read the summary line at the end of the run and note the passed count.

steps.do: Build the chart stylesheet with the Tailwind CLI.

Count the lines in the built CSS that contain the ms-2 logical margin class.

steps.do: Confirm the list demo page exists at the expected path.
Run an accessibility scan of the list page to record the current contrast failures.
Write the targets into the plan: 4.5:1 for list text and 3:1 for row borders and focus rings.
Record the count of color-contrast violations as the baseline the build must bring to zero.

K-002614.example: npx axe reports 3 color-contrast violations in the light theme, all on grey secondary text at 2.9:1. The plan sets 4.5:1 for secondary text, so the build must darken that grey.
K-002614.check: npx axe prints a violations list with the color-contrast rule and ratios below target; the plan records 3 as the starting count.

steps.do: Check whether a token file already defines color custom properties.
Count how many var() references the list stylesheet already uses.
List the minimum pairs: --list-bg, --list-fg, --list-border, --list-hover-bg, and --list-selected-bg, each with a light and a dark value.
Write the five pairs into the plan with a contrast target of 4.5:1 next to each text pair.
Check that the Playwright runner lists tests, so the 4.5:1 contrast check can run in the verify stage.

K-002615.example: rg finds no --list tokens in tokens.css and 0 var() uses in list.css, so the plan adds 5 pairs, such as --list-fg light #1a1a1a and dark #e8e8e8. Each text pair must reach 4.5:1 against its background.
K-002615.check: rg prints no lines for --list tokens on a fresh project, the plan names exactly 5 pairs with a light and dark value each, and npx playwright test --list prints the test names it finds.
traps: Small models define one set of tokens and forget the dark values, so the dark theme inherits light colors. Every token needs both values.
Small models use the same token for hover and selected rows, which hides the selection state. Keep them separate.

steps.do: Find any existing data-theme attribute in the project source.
Find any existing prefers-color-scheme media query in the project source.
List the stylesheets the chosen trigger will have to touch.
Pick prefers-color-scheme as the default and data-theme as a user override that wins over it.
Check that the Playwright runner lists tests, so the default and the override can be verified in a browser.

K-002616.example: rg finds no data-theme hits and no media queries in src, so the plan sets the default with @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) and an override with :root[data-theme='dark']. The override block must come after the media query so it wins at equal specificity.
K-002616.check: rg prints no lines for either pattern on a fresh project, find lists the .css files the build will edit, and npx playwright test --list prints the test names it finds; the plan names one default trigger and one override.
traps: Small models use both triggers without an order, so the media query silently overrides the user's manual choice. Place the override last or raise its specificity.
Small models forget that data-theme must be set on the html element to affect the whole page.

steps.do: Check the head for existing color-scheme lines or theme scripts.
Count the meta color-scheme tags, which should be 0 before the plan adds one.
Locate the closing head tag so the inline script goes above the stylesheet link.
Plan one meta name color-scheme with content light dark and one small inline script that reads localStorage and sets data-theme on the html element before first paint.
Check that the Playwright runner lists tests, so first paint in the saved theme can be checked in a browser before the build is accepted.

K-002617.example: grep -c finds 0 meta tags and grep -n places </head> at index.html:9, so the plan puts the script and meta above line 9. The meta content light dark lets the browser choose native form and scrollbar colors early.
K-002617.check: grep -c prints 0 before the build, npx playwright test --list prints the test names it finds, and after the build grep -c prints 1.
traps: Small models place the script after the stylesheet, so the page paints light first. The script must come before the stylesheet link in head.
Small models use a type=module script, which is deferred and runs after first paint, so the flash remains.

steps.do: Count checkbox inputs in the list markup to size the accent-color work.
Check whether any rule already sets accent-color or appearance on the list.
Plan color-scheme: light dark on :root and accent-color using a theme token on the checkboxes.
Record the checkbox count as the number the verify stage must match against themed checkboxes.
Check that the Playwright runner lists tests, so the 3:1 checkbox contrast can be verified in the verify stage.

K-002618.example: grep -c reports 4 checkboxes in list.html, and rg finds no accent-color rule, so the plan adds accent-color: var(--list-accent) on the list. The token keeps each checkbox at 3:1 or better against the dark row background.
K-002618.check: grep -c prints the checkbox count, rg prints no lines for an unthemed list, npx playwright test --list prints the test names it finds, and the plan names one accent token and one color-scheme line on :root.
traps: Small models set accent-color to a fixed hex, which stays bright and low-contrast in dark mode. Use a var() token instead.
Small models set color-scheme on one list row, which leaves the page scrollbar light. Set it on :root.

steps.do: Create the reports directory for profiler output.
Wrap UserList in React Profiler in src/components/UserList.perf.test.tsx and count onRender calls for one parent state change.
Run the profiler test with Vitest.
Confirm the row commit count is 1 after an unrelated parent state change with 500 rows.

K-002619.example: Mount UserList with 500 users, then set an unrelated filter state in the parent, and the Profiler onRender callback fires once. Before React.memo on UserRow it fired 501 times, which is the failure this card catches.
K-002619.check: Vitest prints 1 passed and the test asserts renderCount equals 1, so the output shows Tests 1 passed (1).
traps: A small model counts only the list render and forgets the row renders, so the expected count must include row components.
Profiler onRender fires per commit, not per component, so do not assert row count from it alone.
Do not change the test data size between runs, or the before and after counts cannot be compared.

steps.do: Confirm the list component imports FixedSizeList from react-window.
Write tests/list-virtualization.spec.ts that loads /users with 10000 items and counts elements with role listitem.
Run the Playwright virtualization test.
Assert the rendered listitem count is 25 or fewer at a 800px viewport height with 40px rows.

K-002620.check: Playwright reports 1 passed, and the count assertion shows the rendered count is at most 25.

Forgetting overscan makes the expected count too strict, so allow a margin of about 5 rows.
Do not use the default 1280px viewport without stating it, since row count depends on height.

steps.do: Create the reports directory for the Lighthouse JSON output.
Run Lighthouse against the built list page at localhost port 4173, limited to the performance category.
Read the performance score from the JSON report.
Confirm the score is 0.9 or higher and the Total Blocking Time audit is under 200ms.

K-002621.check: jq prints a number of 0.9 or higher, for example 0.93.

Lighthouse scores vary by run, so repeat the audit at least three times before deciding.

steps.do: Confirm each row component is wrapped with memo from react in src/components/UserRow.tsx.
Write src/components/UserRow.memo.test.tsx that renders UserList, changes an unrelated prop, and counts row render calls.
Run the memo test with Vitest.
Assert the row render count stays at 500 after the rerender, with no extra renders.

K-002622.check: Vitest reports 1 passed, and the asserted row render count after rerender equals the initial count of 500.

Confirm the map call uses item.id as the key.
Write src/components/UserList.mount.test.tsx that mounts 10000 users and measures time with performance.now.
Run the mount test with Vitest.

K-002623.check: The first grep prints nothing, the second grep prints the key={user.id} line, and Vitest reports 1 passed with mount time at most 200ms.

K-002624.check: Playwright reports 1 passed, and the logged elapsedMs value is 200 or less.

steps.do: Decide the error element id is the input id plus the suffix -error.
Check that no existing file already uses aria-describedby, so the pattern is not duplicated.
Confirm Tailwind ships the aria-invalid variant by searching its installed source.

K-002625.check: rg exits with code 1 and no output, meaning no conflict, and grep lists at least one file under node_modules/tailwindcss/src.

Do not put role alert and aria-live on one node, because screen readers announce the message twice.

steps.do: List the candidate Tailwind color classes for error text and placeholder text.
Search the repo for existing text-red classes so the new styles reuse them.
Keep only text colors whose contrast against white is at least 4.5:1, and border colors at least 3:1.
Confirm the input height class h-11 is used, which is 2.75rem or 44px at a 16px root size.

K-002626.check: The rg output shows text-red-600, and the planned contrast value for error text is 4.5:1 or higher.

steps.do: Name one test per state: empty required, error after blur, and error cleared after typing.
Check that the Playwright config exists before planning the tests.
List the existing test files to match the naming pattern.
Set the error message to appear within 200ms after blur.
Plan the command the build stage will run to prove the states.

K-002627.check: test -f exits with code 0, find lists at least one file, and the planned command includes npx playwright test.

steps.do: Find existing components that render an input element in the source tree.
Read the Tailwind version from package.json to know which variants are available.
Read the Tailwind config file if it exists.
